title: Research: sharp rank-one block budgets and per-block overhead obstruction
head: 488f2ecf1835c6d813e96543656dddf0062fdc9a
body:
The revision-3 rank-shape task needs a complete budget before block-decoder synthesis. This package supplies sharp integer thresholds for reblocking the selected complex word's rank-one payload, with gathering/copy/restoration work charged on top of the old idle bill.

For maximum block rank 16, at least **363 of 2,412 rank-one children per invocation** must be reblocked to pass an optimistic primitive-saving target 5% above the baseline packing-ceiling upper bracket. Full reblocking permits only **10 additional integer rank units**: a single extra rank-16 call fails. For every block rank 2..51 and every saving up to that target, **one additional rank-one call per nontrivial output block erases the local payload saving**. Concavity proves the optimal integer partition and monotone thresholds; exact adjacent signs are retained for all 50 caps. The mass-preserving 1/99 rejection corroborates the predecessor's stronger rank-one-deletion obstruction.

Only `research/complex-rank-one-block-budget/` is added. This is a favorable cost-alphabet relaxation and conditional overhead-tariff obstruction, **no physical decoder, supplier admission or new kappa**. Compatibility, chronological frames, dirty-state realization, compiler/hosting, precision/tape and outer reduction remain unproved. The 5% target concerns the complex primitive ceiling; the selected bit budget would already bind a realized construction there. Full selected cold replay, native execution, Lean, hosted CI and independent human review were not supplied.

Validation passed under Python 3.12.14:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-rank-one-block-budget
```

The retained atanh/Taylor engine and separately written outward-rounded binomial engine agree on the baseline bracket, all 50 thresholds, overhead decisions and block-tax inequalities. Replay checks 10,274 complete small integer partitions and eight mathematical/domain controls. Six tests cover exact-square validation of all 72 square-root oracle bounds, incorrect-oracle rejection, source drift/inventory omission, numeric and bool/int receipt corruption, and optimized read-only relocation. Direct optimized Python 3.14.7 replay and whitespace checks also pass.

Started from current main `adc34159e0d6dc3dd2af2bdba3f5ca7376ef957e`, chooser nonce `3ab0bbddb657f850e7894cfc57f8d29e`, priority revision 3. TASK.json explicitly records the scope change from physical decoder synthesis to its first screening experiment; passing this experiment is not satisfaction of the construction acceptance gate. SOURCES.json pins four live inputs plus historical provenance. Coordination: [Discussion1596](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1596). Pre-submission overlap covered 733 open PRs including drafts and 244 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; coverage does not establish novelty. Refreshed upstream `81e81af6` leaves guidance, selected record and all live input blobs unchanged.

Credit Douglas Colkitt / #1240 for the selected local-word ceiling and ideal-lever model, Sagar Thakrar / #1012 for the coverage law, Rohan Arun / #1094 and #1042, Jeremy Kothe, Hao Yan / FanPUYen, Josie Elliston and the retained construction lineage. #1264 supplies the pending-profile census; Sagar Thakrar's #1334 supplies different bit-side ideal-lever budgets. This package adds partial integer reblocking and a fully additional-work tax. Prepared by **Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, proof, both arithmetic implementations, tests and writing. No subagents. New material is Apache-2.0.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
